surfaces.surface: A tool writes, replaces, moves or deletes a file.
A tool asks for a strictly wider sandbox mode than the session holds.
A tool runs a shell command, and the processes that command starts.
A tool runs a PowerShell command, and the processes that command starts.
surfaces.reason: The guard reviews a configured name list, and its default omits this provider: `frontends/guard/src/policy.ts` — `shellTools: ['bash', 'shell', 'run_command', 'exec']`. `shellCommandOf` in the same file returns `undefined` for any name off that list, so the call reaches the pipeline as “Not a reviewed shell call.” The installed harness does expose the tool and would accept the name: `packages/shell/tool-pwsh/src/index.ts` declares `name: 'pwsh'` with the same command argument as bash — “command: { type: 'string', required: true, description: 'The PowerShell command to execute.' }” — and the persistent provider `packages/shell/tool-pwsh-persistent/src/index.ts` uses that same name. The name is not added here because the classifier is written for POSIX command lines and no test measures it against PowerShell text, so admitting `pwsh` to the default would put every Windows deployment into enforcing review of an unmeasured rule set; a false positive is not free, because enforcement decides (`frontends/guard/src/policy.ts` — “critical denies, high asks, everything else passes”).

surfaces.surface: A tool writes input to a persistent terminal session, and the shell there runs it.
surfaces.reason: No name list can cover it, because the guard reads the reviewed text from one argument name and this tool uses another. `frontends/guard/src/policy.ts` — “const command = args['command']” — while `packages/terminal/tool-terminal/src/index.ts` declares “name: 'terminal_send'” with “text: { type: 'string', required: true, description: 'UTF-8 text to write to the terminal.' }” and submits Enter by default. Adding `terminal_send` to `shellTools` would therefore still produce an unreviewed call. Covering this surface additionally needs the guard to map a tool name to the argument carrying its command text, which widens the configuration surface, and it needs the classifier measured against interactive input rather than whole command lines.

surfaces.surface: A tool runs model-written code in a worker thread.
surfaces.reason: Nothing approves or admits it. The worker is confined — an empty environment, a heap cap, wall-time and busy-time budgets, and a terminated synchronous loop — but the module records that confinement as containment rather than as a gate: `packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts` — “This is containment, not a security boundary: model code has bash-equivalent trust despite an empty environment, a heap cap, measured event-loop busy-time and wall-time budgets.” No approval record gates `run_code` or the workflow worker on these paths. The one server-side brake is a resource budget, not a permission: `frontends/dsh/src/runtime-governance.ts` — “if (activeHeavyTools >= limits.maxConcurrentHeavyTools)”.

surfaces.surface: A model request reaches a tool that a configured MCP server exposes, over stdio or streamable-http.
surfaces.reason: Nothing decides admission. `packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/transport.ts` builds the stdio transport from the configured command, arguments, environment and working directory verbatim, and the streamable-http transport from the configured URL; the only refusals in the package are the serverName pattern (`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/index.ts` — `const SERVER_NAME_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$/`) and a namespace collision. The call is registered into the shared tool registry (`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/tools.ts` — `ctx.tools.register(definition)`), but the only pre-execute listeners that could decide a non-shell name are scoped elsewhere: `frontends/dsh/src/permission-governance.ts` returns immediately unless the session origin is a subagent, and `frontends/guard/src/policy.ts` answers “Not a reviewed shell call.” A search of the package for an approval reference returns nothing.

surfaces.surface: The local Office editor writes the open document back to the workspace.
A caller creates, edits, submits or reviews an enterprise record such as a contact, an inventory item, an order or a task.
A native automation step acts on the operator's desktop.
A plugin that ships client code is mounted into the running application.
A plugin with no client code is mounted into the running application.
surfaces.reason: A host-only dynamic package activates with no request and no approval. The approval block is preceded by an unconditional activation branch: `packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/src/index.ts` — “if (plan.definition.clientCode === undefined) { const started = await this.activate(plan, undefined, false, attempt); if (started.ok) return this.runResponse(plan.plugin, started) }”, while the approval that follows it computes `requiresApproval` from the client-package grants. The package's own test names the behaviour: `packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/tests/runner.spec.ts` — “it('starts a host-only package immediately, with no request and no approval'”.

surfaces.surface: Something writes the harness configuration that selects which plugins and MCP servers load.
surfaces.reason: No writer gate exists. A search across the application, package and frontend trees finds only readers and templates for the user-layer configuration, and the only guidance is a comment in `apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts` — “Edit cordis.patch.yml, not this file.” This matters because the same file chooses the MCP servers of the surface above: mount access and MCP admission are one seam, and neither side of it is gated.

surfaces.surface: A tool, model provider or MCP server opens an outbound network connection to a destination of its own choosing.
surfaces.reason: No destination allow-list exists. Routing is configured (proxy policy) and the sandbox says the subject is outside its scope — `packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/index.ts` — “Network and process visibility are outside this vocabulary.” One refusal does exist and covers one tool only: `web_fetch` rejects a host that resolves to a non-public address (`packages/web/web-fetch-http/src/network.ts` — “throws WebError('WEB_BLOCKED_URL')”), which is an address-class check rather than a permitted-host set. A search for an allow-list across the web, MCP client and LLM packages returns nothing.

surfaces.surface: An update artifact is downloaded and accepted for installation.
